orb.about: Opening-range breakout. Trade the first clean break of the first N minutes' high/low.
orb.other_side: Overnight/early faders and short-term stops resting just past the opening range; momentum from the open's order imbalance carries further than they price in.
orb.proves_it_wrong: Breaks reverse back inside the range more often than they reach 2R, net of costs, across 100+ trades.

vwap.about: VWAP mean reversion. Fade stretched moves away from the day's VWAP, target VWAP.
vwap.other_side: Impatient market orders and stop cascades that push price far from where the day's volume actually traded; liquidity providers get paid to absorb them.
vwap.proves_it_wrong: Stretched moves keep trending (stop hit more than ~40% of the time) or the average win is too small to cover two sides of slippage.

gapfade.about: Gap fade. When a stock gaps 0.75-4% and the first 5 minutes move against the gap, trade toward a partial gap fill.
gapfade.other_side: Overnight/pre-market buyers (or sellers) who chased news and unwind once regular-session liquidity shows the gap was overdone.
gapfade.proves_it_wrong: Confirmed gaps keep extending (stop above the opening high hit more often than the half-fill target), net of costs.

daily.about: Slow lane: daily-bar ETF strategies aimed at compounding, judged against simply holding SPY (same index as VOO). Decisions use data through yesterday's close and trade at today's close.

trend.about: Trend filter. Hold SPY and QQQ (half each) only while each is above its 200-day average; otherwise that half sits in T-bills (BIL). Judged against holding the same 50/50 SPY+QQQ mix.
trend.other_side: Forced and panicked sellers in drawn-out declines; trends persist because big holders de-risk slowly.
trend.proves_it_wrong: Whipsaws cost more than the crashes it avoids: lower return without a clearly smaller drawdown.

momentum.about: Momentum rotation. At each month end, hold the strongest of US stocks, Nasdaq, small caps, international, gold and bonds over the last 6 months, or T-bills if none beat T-bills.
momentum.other_side: Investors who under-react to news and rebalance on a calendar, plus funds that chase late.
momentum.proves_it_wrong: The leader over 6 months doesn't keep leading next month, net of switching costs.

voltarget.about: Volatility targeting. Hold more SPY when markets are calm and less when they're wild, aiming for about 15% yearly volatility; the rest in T-bills.
voltarget.other_side: Volatility clusters: wild days follow wild days, and leveraged/levered-down holders are forced to trade into it.
voltarget.proves_it_wrong: Cutting exposure after volatile stretches misses the rebounds that follow and doesn't reduce drawdowns.

options.about: Options lane: sell monthly options on one liquid stock whose 100 shares cost $1,000 or less (strike <= $10). Option prices are modeled with Black-Scholes from the stock's own recent volatility, scaled by how expensive its real options were (measured from Alpaca option data since Feb 2024).

wheel.about: The wheel. Sell a ~monthly cash-secured put about 5% below the price; if assigned, sell ~monthly covered calls at least 5% above the price and not below what you paid; when called away, start over.
wheel.other_side: Buyers of crash insurance and lottery-ticket calls, who historically pay more for options than the moves that follow.
wheel.proves_it_wrong: Collected premium doesn't make up for being stuck holding a falling stock and capping the rebounds.

covered_call.about: Covered calls. Hold 100 shares and sell a ~monthly call about 5% above the price; if called away, buy back in at the next cycle.
covered_call.other_side: Call buyers paying up for upside.
covered_call.proves_it_wrong: Capped rallies cost more than the premiums collected.

csp.about: Cash-secured puts only. Sell a ~monthly put about 5% below the price; if assigned, sell the shares at the next cycle and keep selling puts.
csp.proves_it_wrong: Assignments on falling stocks lose more than the premiums collected.
